answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF through a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with only a compact proof verified afterward. Since each square depends on the preceding result, GPUs cannot parallelize one identity’s delay; creating clones multiplies the required wall-clock computation. The tide of Sybil attempts meets a computational bridge, and even ferrous hardware cannot eliminate this physical sequential bottleneck.
